measurement: python3 -m traceability validate — specs + links only, no stand, no network, no test run (scripts/check-traceability-ratchet.py recomputes both numbers from the same package that renders the matrix)
commit: gazon1/sing#3115 — removed the Android flow that asserted the unreachable system-calendar state; retagged calendar_sync/03 as scenario:CAL-SYNC-SYSTEM-02

floors.label: claimed (scenario, target) cells with no automation
floors.note: Lowered 107 -> 93 on 2026-10-27 when feature 016's android carriers landed: the Maestro flows under Maestro/flows/{plans,menu,nav}/ now cover every one of the feature's eighteen scenarios on Android as well as on the desktop, and the desktop flow tests under desktopApp/src/jvmTest/.../flows/{plans,menu,desktop}/ carry the desktop tier. Before, the feature's eleven android cells were holes; they are carriers now. The two android cells that remain dark across the matrix are upstream's. Lowered 93 -> 83 on 2026-10-28 when ten Maestro flows declared the scenario their own spec header named as their carrier: the six `negative/` empty-state flows (NEGATIVE-01..06), `pomodoro/02`, `pomodoro/03` and `pomodoro/05` (POMODORO-02, -03, -05) and `system/search-finds-task` (SEARCH-01). The specs named those flows as their carriers and the flows did not carry the tag, so ten scenarios the repository had already written down read as uncovered. The claims are the flows' own behaviour — the empty states, the chip that starts the timer, the pause and resume, the stop that resets, the search that finds a task by its title. Lowered 83 -> 74 on 2026-10-29 when twelve more flows carried the id their own headers already named: the tag was written bare (`- AUTH-FIRSTRUN-01`) instead of prefixed (`- scenario:AUTH-FIRSTRUN-01`), so the scanner skipped them and the scenarios read as uncovered. Eleven of them (AUTH-FIRSTRUN-01/04/05, AUTH-SIGNIN-01, AUTH-SIGNUP-01, AUTH-ATTACH-01, CAL-SYNC-PROVIDER-01, SYNC-SETTINGS-01, TASK-TIME-01) had specs already; the three AUTH-FAIL scenarios got theirs now, transcribed from the preconditions and steps their flow headers had written down. Lowered 74 -> 73 when the desktop carrier for SYNC-SETTINGS-01 landed (#1394): the scenario now has a carrier on both tiers, and the android cell it had opened is covered again. Lowered 72 -> 71 on 2026-11-05 when the desktop carrier for SYNC-INCOMING-01 landed: the scenario is defined by two devices talking to each other, and the desktop tier now has them — two app instances against one shared server — so the cell it had opened is covered again. Lowered 71 -> 69 on 2026-11-23 with gazon1/sing#3115: two cells, both in the calendar-sync system area. One was CAL-SYNC-SYSTEM-02/android, which was dark because the flow that exercises it carried the bare id `CAL-SYNC-SYSTEM-01` as a tag instead of `scenario:CAL-SYNC-SYSTEM-02`, so no carrier was ever resolved; the tag is fixed and the cell is covered. The other was CAL-SYNC-SYSTEM-01/android, which claimed that the panel shows the 'system calendar unavailable' message on Android — a state Android cannot reach, since the panel's unavailable branch is gated on `deviceSyncSupported` and every one of its four seams is real on Android. The claim was withdrawn rather than kept as a hole: an unreachable guarantee is not a hole to be closed, it is a specification of a behaviour that does not exist. The Android flow that asserted it (calendar_sync/02-system-calendar-unavailable) failed in every sampled run and was removed; the guarantee itself is owned on the desktop tier by CalendarSyncSystemScenarioTest.

floors.label: declared scenarios with a claimed target and no automation on any target
floors.note: Lowered 72 -> 70 on 2026-10-27 with the same carriers: every one of feature 016's eighteen scenarios now has automation on at least one target. The two that remain dark are upstream's. Lowered 70 -> 60 on 2026-10-28 with the same ten carriers: each of the ten scenarios now has automation on at least one target, and its flow says so in a tag rather than only in the spec's header. Lowered 60 -> 54 on 2026-10-29 with the twelve bare-tag flows: six scenarios that had a spec, a claim and a flow that exercised it were dark only because the tag was missing its `scenario:` prefix. Lowered 53 -> 52 on 2026-11-05 with the desktop carrier for SYNC-INCOMING-01: the scenario had a claim and no automation on either tier, and it now has a carrier on the desktop — two app instances against one shared server are the two devices the scenario is defined by. Lowered 52 -> 51 on 2026-11-23 with gazon1/sing#3115: CAL-SYNC-SYSTEM-02 was dark because the flow that exercises it on Android (`calendar_sync/03-system-calendar-toggle.yaml`) carried the bare id `CAL-SYNC-SYSTEM-01` as its tag instead of `scenario:CAL-SYNC-SYSTEM-02`, so the scanner never resolved a carrier for it. The scenario, its spec and its flow all existed and the flow had been passing; only the link was missing. The tag now names the scenario it actually verifies.

floors.label: claimed cells whose spec declares the tier unable to reach them
floors.note: These are counted in `holes` as well, so reclassifying an ordinary hole as unreachable does not move the total — which is the point, and also the hole this floor closes. Without it, marking every unsupplied claim `unreachable` would make the queue look un-actionable while the number stayed at 32, and the cheap move is always the one that leaves the metric alone. The two metrics together mean a reclassification has to be paid for in one bucket or the other. The 6 are the three sync scenarios that are *defined* by a second device (SYNC-INCOMING-01, SYNC-OFFLINE-01, SYNC-PROFILES-01) on both tiers; the rest of the sync area is one-device and stays probe-able. Raised 6 -> 9 on 2026-10-07 by three cells: CAL-SYNC-RECUR-01 on both tiers (needs a second Google account) and CAL-SYNC-SYSTEM-01 on android only (the panel's 'system calendar unavailable' branch is gated on `deviceSyncSupported`, and every one of its four seams is real on Android, so the branch is unreachable there by construction; desktop reaches the branch by construction and IS claimed). Corrected 2026-11-23: this cell was recorded as the 'permission denied' branch, which was wrong — denying READ_CALENDAR shows the permission gate, not the unavailable message. Lowered 9 -> 8 on 2026-11-05 when the desktop carrier for SYNC-INCOMING-01 landed: the desktop cell was unreachable because a single-device harness cannot express a conflict between two devices, and the two-instance desktop harness can — one shared server, two app instances, two databases. The android cell stays unreachable, because the android tier has no second device to be the other side of the conflict. Lowered 8 -> 7 on 2026-11-23 with gazon1/sing#3115: the CAL-SYNC-SYSTEM-01/android cell is gone, because the scenario no longer claims android at all. The cell was not closed — it was withdrawn: the 'system calendar unavailable' panel cannot be reached on Android, so it was never a hole waiting for a carrier, it was a claim about a state that does not exist. The Android guarantee that does exist — the permission gate shown when READ/WRITE_CALENDAR is not granted — has no test tag and no carrier yet; it is named in the CAL-SYNC-SYSTEM-01 spec as the reachable state this scenario does not cover.

known_gaps: The calendar-sync panel carried ZERO test tags until 2026-10-07, which is the concrete form this gap takes: not a missing test but a missing ADDRESS. No automation could have reached any of its user-visible behaviour regardless of how the ViewModel was tested, so '23 unit-test classes' and '0 carriers' were both true and not in tension. Tags were added alongside TestTags.CalendarSync; and SettingsSwitchRow's testTag parameter — which defaulted to TestTags.Settings.DARK_THEME_SWITCH — is now required, because 15 of its 16 call sites were silently inheriting the dark-theme tag, which makes onNodeWithTag throw on multiple matches.

16 android cells are holes and stay holes on a host with no device: the tier is unverifiable here, and that is more than half the matrix. docs/testing/android-tier-runbook.md is the work order. Because every android hole is 1-for-1, no desktop work can move the total by more than 1; the android tier is where the count is.

The android column of the result matrix is not filled by CI, deliberately. `:androidApp:connectedDebugAndroidTest` ran in no CI job until android-device-tests.yml added it on 2026-10-07 (nightly, tags, manual, and the `run-device-tests` PR label) — but that job produces instrumentation reports, not Maestro scenario results, so it does not move this column. `traceability results --maestro` would need a `scenario:` tag on every flow that claims android — 18 of 19 specs claim it and exactly one flow (TASK-REC-01) carries the tag. CI therefore normalises `--targets desktop` only, so the android cells read as a deliberate `not-run` instead of looking like a measurement that happened to be empty. To close it, tag the flows — the instrumentation job is necessary but not sufficient, which is why the gap stays. See docs/decisions/2026-10-07-the-instrumentation-tier-ran-in-no-ci-job.md.
